column1: # linkmetric group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B02). Builder A, 2026-11-20.
# Sources: IEEE 1905.1 through the usp-spec MCP server (doc ieee1905): §6.4 (TLV header; no byte-order statement),
#   TLV codes from the tables (8, 9, 10, 12, 18, 19) match em-types codes.rs:249-253, 259-260.
#   343 (0x12), 344 (0x13); all port_rule SPEC (321 answered in note 0009 D3). Note 0009 D2 (raw reserved
#   values, zero counts), D3 line 321, D4 (2-octet query is a spec form, no lenient forms in this group).
# Wire layouts (hex = tlvValue only; multi-octet integers big-endian, as B01 and audit 322 for 1905.1):
#   0x08: [0] selector, then either [1] metrics (2 octets total, selector 0 only) or [1..7) neighbor AL MAC,
#         [7] metrics (8 octets, any selector; the MAC is kept as found when the selector is 0). D3 line 321.
#         Selector 0x02-0xff and metrics 0x03-0xff are reserved and carried raw (D2).
#   0x09: [0..6) local AL MAC, [6..12) neighbor AL MAC, then links x 29 octets, no count octet (audit 323):
#         local if MAC(6), neighbor if MAC(6), intfType(2), IEEE802.1BridgeFlag(1), packetErrors(4),
#   0x0a: [0..6) local AL MAC, [6..12) neighbor AL MAC, then links x 23 octets, no count octet (audit 326):
#         local if MAC(6), neighbor if MAC(6), intfType(2), packetErrors(4), packetsReceived(4), rssi(1) (Tables 6-19/6-20).
#   0x0c: [0] result code; exactly 1 octet (Table 6-21). 0x00 Invalid neighbor, 0x01-0xff reserved, carried raw (D2).
#   0x12: [0] n, then n x { intfType(2), k(1), media-specific info(k) } (Table 6-27); n may be 0 (table: "can be 0").
#         Info is raw bytes sized by k; media type vs k is not checked by the codec (D2). 802.11 info per Table 6-13.
#   0x13: [0..6) AL ID, [6..8) MID, [8..14) transmitting-interface MAC, [14..20) new-device interface MAC; exactly 20
# Field notes: links/media are list lengths; for 0x09/0x0a links is not on the wire. m0_info_len overrides k.
#   `trailing`/`partial` are extra raw bytes appended after the listed fields. A field given as hex: where the case
#   normally takes a MAC/integer is a cut field (raw bytes as written); a listed entry field that is left out
#   (missing-rssi, missing-info-length) is absent from the bytes. Counters are decimal; codes are 0x-hex.

# Choices: (1) zero-links (0x09, 0x0a) is kind=invalid, error=InvalidLength: Tables 6-17/6-19 say "n can be one or more" (spec explicit, note 0009 D8); corrected by the coordinator 2026-11-20 (the D2 zero-count rule covers count fields that may be 0, not these).
#   (2) Every cut field, partial entry or overstated count/length is error=Truncated, as in B01.
#   (3) 0x08 with a non-zero selector and 2 octets (specific-without-mac, selector-reserved-without-mac) is
#   Truncated: D3 line 321 accepts 2 octets only with selector 0. (4) 0x08 encoder: the 2-octet form for selector 0
#   without a MAC, 8 octets whenever a neighbor MAC is present (D3 line 321).
# bridge-reserved (0x02), link-availability-over-100 (101), metrics/selector/result reserved values and
#   media-80211-info-empty are spec cases: raw values carried as found (D2).
